1.pericope_label: Zedekiah sends Pashur and Zephaniah: enquire of the Lord for us, that Nebuchadrezzar may go up from us
debates: Whether the embassy was sincere or a trap
Where this chapter belongs in the order of the book
What kind of man Zedekiah was
outliers: Calvin says the messengers wished God honestly consulted and were convinced of the integrity of Jeremiah, where Ellicott takes the mission for an attempt to entice him into siding with the war party
themes: A prophecy standing out of its own order
A king who humbles himself only as far as it costs him nothing
A request that the enemy leave rather than that God return
A covenant pleaded by those who broke it

3.pericope_label: Thus saith the Lord God of Israel: I will turn back the weapons in your hands, and I myself will fight against you
debates: What the turning back of the weapons means
Whether the three words for anger form a deliberate gradation
Why the answer offers no opening for repentance
outliers: Calvin renders the verb of the fourth verse I prohibit, reporting but not adopting the rendering I will turn them against you which Clarke and Keil and Delitzsch assume
themes: A message sent back rather than carried to the king
A divine title quoted against those who claim it
God named as the commander of the besieging army
Severity defended as the only thing that could wake a king

6.pericope_label: I will smite the inhabitants of this city, man and beast: Zedekiah given into the hand of Nebuchadrezzar
debates: Whether the pestilence is a natural consequence of the siege or an immediate act of God
Why the beasts are included in the judgment
What is meant by those that are left in the city
outliers: Clarke distinguishes the pestilence from the sword as the immediate act of God, where Ellicott grants it the ordinary consequence of a siege before reading it providentially
themes: A plague read as both epidemic and verdict
Innocent animals used to measure human guilt
Endurance under siege declared useless in advance
A prophecy spoken against a king still on his throne

8.pericope_label: I set before you the way of life and the way of death: he that goeth out to the Chaldeans shall have his life for a prey
debates: What the verb rendered falleth to the Chaldeans means
What it is to have life for a prey
Whether anyone acted on the advice to surrender
outliers: Ellicott says not a few in fact went out to the Chaldeans as advised, where Henry says that for aught that appears few or none took the counsel
Calvin rejects two renderings of the verb outright, saying that those who make it died touch neither heaven nor earth
themes: A famous offer of life and death quoted in its narrowest sense
Counsel that could not be distinguished from treason
Survival described as loot carried off a battlefield
A city burned where conquerors usually preferred to keep it

11.pericope_label: To the house of the king of Judah: O house of David, execute judgment in the morning lest my fury go out like fire
debates: Whether these verses belong to the siege or to an earlier reign
Why the house of David is addressed by that name
Whether judgment in the morning is a literal hour or a figure for promptness
outliers: Gill takes the name of David as an appeal to a great ancestor example, where Calvin says it is used not for honour but in contempt, and dismisses the other reading as unmeaning
Keil and Delitzsch report three scholars who detach the passage from the siege entirely, and Ellicott lays out both sides without deciding
themes: A conditional offer set beside a sentence already passed
A covenant treated as a private exemption
The morning hour as the test of a just king
Mitigated wrath called a great thing

13.pericope_label: Behold, I am against thee, O inhabitant of the valley: I will kindle a fire in the forest thereof
debates: What the valley and the rock of the plain are
What the forest that is to burn stands for
Who speaks the boast about none coming down against us
outliers: Ellicott divides the two phrases between the lower and the higher city, where Calvin and Wesley take both of one place
Clarke rejects outright a rendering that makes the phrase the levelled hollow of a rock, saying he cannot see the good sense of it
themes: A city defended by the shape of its own ground
A phrase the versions could not agree how to render
Timber that becomes the fuel of the house it built
Security named as the thing God most hates
